provenance: Stage-2 lane split applying the decision-agent's documented routing rule (detect-vs-hunt by detection feasibility, not severity: low=hunt, medium/high=detect) deterministically from each TTP's Stage-1 detection_feasibility assessment. Partition validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup; all ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — inbound links to newly-registered/look-alike domains are detectable via email-security URL analysis, proxy/DNS logging and user-reported phishing, but tailored lures on cloud infrastructure evade generic filtering
medium — credential-harvest landing pages are detectable via URL/domain reputation and post-submission anomalous logons, but the collection itself happens on attacker infrastructure
medium — link clicks are observable via proxy/DNS and browser telemetry, but distinguishing a malicious job-site click from normal browsing requires domain reputation context
medium — execution of a downloaded payload is detectable via process-creation and download-provenance (mark-of-the-web) telemetry, though the initial dropper varies per campaign
medium — valid-account logons are detectable via identity analytics (impossible travel, new device/geo, atypical MFA) but blend with legitimate access without behavioral baselining

medium — third-party/VDI access is detectable via monitoring of vendor accounts, VDI session anomalies and unexpected process launches inside brokered sessions, but requires visibility into the trust boundary and the VDI layer

high — a legitimate signed binary loading an unsigned/unexpected DLL from a non-standard path (e.g. VGAuthCLI.exe loading VGAuth.dll from a writable dir, files under VMware VGAuth) is detectable via module-load (Sysmon EID 7) and signature/path-mismatch analytics; this is the strongest endpoint surface for the actor

medium — signed malware evades trust controls, but the specific signing certificates (once identified/revoked) and signer-reputation anomalies are detectable via certificate-thumbprint watchlists and code-integrity telemetry
medium — files masquerading inside trusted product directories and service-like C2 hostnames are detectable via path/name baselining and file-integrity monitoring of vendor software folders

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Dynamic API Resolution
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — dynamic API resolution and string obfuscation are detectable via YARA/behavioral analysis (e.g. GetProcAddress loops, XOR string decoding) but require memory/behavioral inspection rather than static AV

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — high-entropy/encoded artifacts (XOR-encrypted .jpg screenshots under Users\Public) are detectable via file-entropy and content analytics with dedicated scanning
medium — rapid file-creation-then-deletion of executables is detectable via file-system and EDR delete-event telemetry, but the window is short and requires continuous recording

high — deletion of the Terminal Server Client\Default and \Servers registry keys is a specific, high-fidelity command detectable via process command-line and registry-modification (Sysmon EID 12/13) telemetry

high — DCSync generates directory-replication requests (DRSUAPI DsGetNCChanges / Event ID 4662 with replication GUIDs) from non-DC principals, a high-fidelity identity detection; the LOG.txt output paths add host-level corroboration
high — password spraying (many accounts, few passwords, from a small set of sources) is detectable via authentication-failure fan-out analytics (Event ID 4625 / Azure AD sign-in logs)

detection_candidates.technique_name: Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
detection_candidates.rationale: high — bursts of Kerberos TGS requests (Event ID 4769) with RC4 encryption for many SPNs from one host are a well-established Kerberoasting detection

medium — anomalous certificate enrollment (AD CS Event IDs 4886/4887) and RBCD/msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity modifications are detectable via CA and directory auditing, but require AD CS logging to be enabled

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: high — access to browser credential stores plus CryptUnprotectData usage and token impersonation of explorer.exe are detectable via EDR API/behavioral telemetry; the crash.log/config.txt paths add corroboration
medium — spurious credential-prompt processes and cleartext credential files are detectable via process/UI and file-write telemetry, but the fake dialog itself may resemble legitimate auth prompts
medium — net user/net group enumeration is detectable via command-line logging but is common admin activity; value comes from recon-burst/process-lineage correlation
medium — AD Explorer execution and bulk LDAP/directory queries are detectable via process and directory-service query auditing, but need baselining against legitimate admin use
medium — internal RDP (Type-10 logon 4624) fan-out and session activity is detectable via authentication and RDP-session analytics, but blends with legitimate admin RDP without baselining

detection_candidates.technique_name: Remote Service Session Hijacking: RDP Hijacking
detection_candidates.rationale: high — RDP session hijacking (session reconnect to another user's session, SYSTEM-context tscon) produces distinctive session-change and logon events (4778/4779) that are high-fidelity when baselined
medium — WinRM/PowerShell Remoting is detectable via WinRM operational logs and wsmprovhost.exe process lineage, but overlaps with legitimate remote administration
medium — abuse of SCCM Remote Control is detectable via SCCM audit logs, CmRcService activity, and unexpected remote-control sessions, but requires SCCM-specific monitoring
high — unsanctioned RMM/remote tools (AWRC, ZeroTier, ngrok) are detectable via process/known-binary signatures, install events and outbound connections to their service endpoints
medium — anomalous SharePoint/Teams access and bulk downloads are detectable via M365 audit (unified audit log) analytics for unusual principals/volumes, but require cloud-app logging
high — periodic creation of timestamped image files under Users\Public\Videos|Music by a non-standard process is a specific, high-fidelity file-creation detection

medium — HTTPS beaconing to Azure blends with normal cloud traffic, but the hardcoded /news URI, /register/ endpoint, static User-Agent and JSON registration body are detectable via proxy/TLS-metadata and web-log analytics when combined with the actor domain list

medium — tunneler processes side-loaded via legitimate binaries plus outbound proxy connections to Azure are detectable via process-execution and network telemetry when correlated with the DLL-hijack host and actor domains

high — Windows ssh.exe launched with reverse-tunnel flags (-R) to port 443 and StrictHostKeyChecking=no is an anomalous, high-fidelity command-line/process detection on Windows endpoints, corroborated by outbound 443 to the tunnel IPs
medium — file writes following backdoor C2 activity are detectable via process+file telemetry and download-provenance, but the encrypted Azure channel obscures the transfer itself

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — off-victim social-media reconnaissance and recruiter outreach are not endpoint-observable; intel/brand-monitoring and employee-awareness candidate

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Gather Victim Network Information: IP Addresses
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — reconnaissance conducted from within already-compromised mailboxes/third parties is largely invisible to the ultimate victim; hunt candidate via mailbox audit logs on compromised tenants
low — domain registration is off-victim; intel/hunt candidate via newly-registered-domain and look-alike-domain monitoring

low — the C2 is hosted on legitimate Azure infrastructure that resolves and TLS-terminates like any benign cloud service; hunt-leaning via curated actor-domain blocklists, JA3/TLS and rare-Azure-tenant beaconing analytics rather than a generic signature
low — capability development is off-victim; per-sample unique hashing specifically defeats IOC-hash matching, pushing detection toward behavior/YARA — intel candidate
low — certificate acquisition is off-victim; the downstream signed-binary execution is where detection lands (see T1553.002) — intel candidate
low — TLS on 443 to Azure is ubiquitous and content is opaque; hunt-leaning via TLS-fingerprint (JA3/JA3S), beacon-periodicity and destination-reputation analytics rather than payload inspection
low — exfiltration rides the same encrypted Azure C2 as beaconing and blends with normal cloud egress; hunt-leaning via volumetric/egress-anomaly analytics tied to the actor domains
